title: Primary-source hard-gate audit of published VZAA formulation

source.title: Vadose zone analytical algorithm (VZAA): a non-iterative algorithm for vadose zone soil moisture and groundwater recharge

published_algorithm_reconstruction.hydraulic_model_statement: Article states that any h-theta-K-D hydraulic model may be used; study uses van Genuchten relationships
important_derivation_approximations: total moisture gradient decomposed into downward surface-flux and upward groundwater-flux contributions
diffusion equation used instead of full Richards equation to estimate moisture gradient
D(theta) treated as constant in the fractional-derivative derivation
steady upward-flow term derived assuming exponential K(h)

published_mass_balance_evidence.paper_statement: non-negligible residuals remain for large spatial and temporal steps

published_bottom_boundary_evidence.reason: current non-iterative surface-driven formulation does not explicitly enforce a prescribed lower boundary
published_bottom_boundary_evidence.paper_interpretation: non-zero residual bottom flux can create artificial gains or losses

layered_soil_evidence.paper_attribution: Eq. 3 analytical flux model was derived for uniform rather than layered soil

reason: fails SWAP5 exact discrete mass-conservation requirement as published
fails SWAP5 explicit prescribed bottom head/flux boundary requirement as published

next_required_actions: capture and provenance-check the DOI-linked supplementary MATLAB appendices before claiming code reproduction
reproduce at least one published case without modifying the official code
write a layer-by-layer conservation ledger for the exact published update
prove or disprove whether one bounded correction can enforce an explicit bottom head or flux while preserving the same accepted-step mass ledger
test whether any correction remains O(N_layers) or bounded O(N_layers * N_corrections)
separate donor concepts from any claim that the published VZAA solver itself is admitted
